body:
## Summary
Every number on the Brain floors comes from a client-side fold over a page window: Layer 1 reads 6,000 ledger rows and 2,000 runs, Engine reads 5,000 rows, and each folds its own sample. Past 5,000 calls the two floors give two different totals for one tournament, and both label the gap '(first pages)'. Add `ledger.summary`, a daemon method over the same source grammar as `ledger.page` (run, tournament or the daemon ledger). It folds every complete row once and returns the totals, per-role routes and per-account rows that engineModel computes today. The floors render the summary. The paged ledger stays for the table and the lanes only.

## Description
The technique is metrics-rollups / bundle-endpoints: numbers read together are computed together, in one scan and under one predicate, and a failed section is shown as failed rather than as empty. Today the Brain page has two endpoints in disguise: two windows, two folds, and two answers to 'how many calls'. measurement-honesty / unmeasurable-vs-zero covers the cost field. The summary counts `uncosted_calls` beside `cost_usd`, so the StatBand can say '$x + n uncosted' and stop showing a silent $0. The summary keeps engineModel's definitions exactly: failed calls are left out of the duration percentiles, and percentiles are nearest-rank through reconcile `stats::percentile`. It also streams lines with the `complete_lines` rule ledger.page uses, so one source has one interpretation. The browser keeps a fallback: if `ledger.summary` errors, the floors fold the window as they do now and keep the '(first pages)' label. The method is additive and reads the same files, so nothing new is stored or exposed (accounts stay labels only, per LedgerEntry's doc). The recorded bounded-enumeration deviation (offset resume, Engine.tsx:112) is left alone. This card stops depending on that path for totals, and does not fix it.

## Flow
- types: `LedgerSummaryParams { run_id?, tournament_id? }`, `LedgerSummary { calls, errors, fallbacks, cost_usd, uncosted_calls, unrouted, routes: [RouteSummary], accounts: [AccountSummary] }`, register `ledger.summary`
- daemon paging.rs: `ledger_summary` reuses `ledger_files` + line parsing, folds per role/account, and computes percentiles with reconcile stats. rpc.rs dispatch. e2e over a >5,000-row tournament
- regenerate the contract
- console: engineModel adapts LedgerSummary -> EngineSummary (one adapter, so EngineFloor is unchanged). Engine and useBrain read `ledger.summary` for totals, roles and lamps. Layer1 runs come from the TournamentRow. invalidation adds ledger.summary on stream_end/segment_end/job
- tests: testgen's scripted daemon answers ledger.summary from its generated season

## Expected impact
The Brain floors give one true call, error, fallback and cost total for any tournament size, and the same number on both floors. Engine stops re-reading the tournament's ledger 10 times to produce a sample. Unknown cost becomes visible instead of reading as zero. The page windows keep their real job: the drawn lanes and the browsable table.

## Evaluation
Claim: a daemon-side summary makes the Brain's totals whole-source and consistent across floors.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no ledger.summary method; Engine reads 5,000 and Layer1 reads 6,000 of 9,000; missing cost folds to $0)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (daemon e2e + console scripted season)
Result: better
Gate: contract (additive method in shadowrunr-types / packages/contract) + architecture

"Engine calls (first pages)" : "Engine calls"` | brainModel.ts:237 `calls: ledger.length, runs: runs.length` | engineModel.ts:61 `cost += l.cost_usd ?? 0;` | paging.rs:271-283 `'files: for file in ledger_files(cfg, &p)? { let lines = complete_lines(&file.path)?; if skip >= lines.len() ... skip -= ...` | types rpc.rs:212-213 `pub instrument_hash: String, pub runs: usize,` | grep 'ledger.summary' over crates/ packages/ apps/ -> 0 hits

critic.reason: True premise, honest L, and sharp cases at a scale that exceeds both windows. Sequence it before brain-page B.

body:
## Summary
The operator changes routes, tiers, accounts or the character, runs a tournament, and opens the Engine floor to see if the engine got faster or flakier. The floor shows one ledger. To answer the question the operator flips the source select back and forth and remembers the p95s. Add a 'Compare with' baseline. By default it is the previous tournament. The routing table then gains a per-role delta view: calls, error rate in pp, p50, p95 and first-text p50 in ms, plus fallbacks and cost. Both sides are named, and a delta only shows where the sample can carry it.

## Description
The technique is diff-comparison / pair-and-baseline-selection. The baseline is the question, here a temporal one: 'what changed since the last tournament?'. So the pair appears above the rows, and the sides are named by role (baseline and candidate), not as left and right. diff-honesty applies too: if either window is truncated, the compare says it is partial and does not present the delta as whole-source. measurement-honesty / minimum-sample-floors applies as well: a role below minN shows 'too few calls', not a p95 swing built on 12 calls. A role present on one side only is 'new' or 'gone', never a delta against zero. When instrument_hash differs, the compare carries a caution, as the simulator does. `compareSummaries(base, cand, {minN})` is a pure function next to summariseLedger, and EngineCompare renders its rows with Chip tones (worse=caution, better=ok). The baseline ledger uses the same usePaged window as the source. If card A lands, both sides read ledger.summary and the partial note disappears, but this card does not depend on it. No contract change, and nothing new is stored.

## Flow
- Engine: `compareTo` state. Default is the tournament before the source in the tournaments page, or none for the daemon ledger. A 'Compare with' select sits next to 'Ledger'
- second usePaged('ledger.page', baseParams, STEP) only when compareTo is set, then summariseLedger on both
- engineModel.compareSummaries -> rows {role, state: both|new|gone|thin, base, cand, deltas, direction}
- EngineCompare: header (baseline id, candidate id, partial, instrument note) and a table with data-role brain-compare
- tests: pure model tests and a scripted-season UI test

## Expected impact
The question the Engine floor exists to answer ('did my change make the engine better?') takes one glance instead of select-flipping from memory. Regressions in p95 or error rate per role become visible right after the tournament that caused them.

## Evaluation
Claim: a named-baseline per-role compare answers the before/after question on the Engine floor.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no compareSummaries, no Compare control, no brain-compare surface)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: none (in-scope console feature, no contract change)
